method: ZIP (2020 ZCTA) to Texas House district, joined through 2020 Census tabulation blocks. Blocks nest inside both, so this is an ID join, not a polygon intersection: no boundary slivers. Where a ZIP spans districts, every district it touches is listed with its share of the ZIP POPULATION at the 2020 census, most people first, and its share of the ZIP land area beside it. Ordering by land instead put a different district first in 108 of the 913 split ZIPs. Nothing is pruned — the reader picks from the list, so a surplus entry is cheaper than a missing one.

sources.blockToDistrictNote: 2022 plan, not the 2020 Block Assignment File: 33% of Texas blocks changed district between them.
sources.blockToPopulationNote: P.L. 94-171 table P1, field P0010001, joined to the geographic header on LOGRECNO at SUMLEV 750. The block populations total the published state figure of 29,145,505.

format: zips[zip] is a district number when the ZIP lies in one district, or an array of [district, people, percent of ZIP land area] triples, most people first. PEOPLE IS A HEAD COUNT, not a percent: its 2020 census residents of the part of this ZIP inside that district, and the counts for a ZIP sum to its population. A count rather than a share so that nobody-lives-there and almost-nobody-lives-there stay distinguishable. The land percent is published for audit, not for ranking.
